binders: A type Ω equipped with a measurable-space structure.
A measure μ on Ω equipped with an IsProbabilityMeasure μ instance.
An indexed family X : ι → Ω → ℝ of real-valued functions.
Two endpoint functions m,M : ι → ℝ.
hypotheses: For every i ∈ ι, X_i is measurable from Ω to the Borel real line.
The indexed family X satisfies ProbabilityTheory.iIndepFun X μ, conventionally independence with respect to μ.
For every i ∈ ι, X_i(ω) belongs to the closed interval [m_i,M_i] for μ-almost every ω.
The threshold is strictly positive: 0 < t.
conclusions: Let A_t = {ω ∈ Ω | ∑_{i∈ι}(X_i(ω) - ∫_Ω X_i(y) dμ(y)) ≥ t}. Then (μ(A_t)).toReal ≤ exp((-2 t^2)/(∑_{i∈ι}|M_i-m_i|^2)).
mathematical_definitions: For each i, the centering constant is the real-valued integral ∫_Ω X_i dμ.
The centered finite sum is S(ω) = ∑_{i∈ι}(X_i(ω) - ∫_Ω X_i dμ).
The tail event is A_t = {ω | S(ω) ≥ t}.
The notation μ.real(A_t) in the target means (μ(A_t)).toReal.
translation.proposition_plain_english: For any finite family of measurable real-valued functions on a probability space that is independent with respect to μ and whose ith member lies μ-almost surely between m_i and M_i, and for every positive t, the real-valued measure of the event that the sum of the functions minus their μ-integrals is at least t is at most exp(-2t² divided by the sum of the squared interval widths |M_i-m_i|²).

restrictions_and_vacuity_risks: The index type is only required to be finite and may be empty.

Each bound is an individual μ-almost-everywhere assertion. Because ι is finite these can conventionally be combined into one common full-measure set, but the target does not state that combined event explicitly.

There is no explicit assumption m_i ≤ M_i. If m_i > M_i for some i, the closed interval is empty; under the intended probability-measure semantics its a.e. membership hypothesis cannot hold, so that case makes the implication vacuous.

There is no explicit assumption that V = ∑_{i∈ι}|M_i-m_i|² is positive. Real division in Lean is totalized: when V = 0, (-2t²)/V is 0, so the stated right side is exp(0)=1 rather than a limiting value involving negative infinity.
The conclusion is a one-sided upper-tail statement using ≥ t; it does not state a lower-tail or two-sided bound.
The left side uses ENNReal.toReal through Measure.real. The probability-measure assumption is intended to ensure finiteness, but its exact definition is not expanded in the dossier.

No separate integrability hypothesis is present. The a.e. finite interval bounds together with the intended probability-measure semantics should imply integrability, but the integral operator itself is total and its exact fallback behavior is not exposed by the supplied body.
Independence is asserted by iIndepFun relative to μ; the one-level body delegates to a kernel-level predicate whose exact semantics are not supplied.
ambiguities: The dossier gives only the type of IsProbabilityMeasure, so its precise normalization field or condition is not independently visible.
The body of MeasureTheory.integral is opaque at the supplied boundary, so its exact definition and nonintegrable-case convention cannot be reconstructed from this packet alone.

The body of iIndepFun delegates to ProbabilityTheory.Kernel.iIndepFun, whose definition is absent, so the exact formal independence semantics cannot be reconstructed beyond the conventional indexed-independence reading.
